localContributorCensus.rules: Require exactly one author plus every worker that finished or edited implementation, each role author or finisher; zero finishers is represented by the census containing only its author, not an omitted identity contract. Author and finishers may coincide only by one deduplicated actor entry; reviewer may coincide with neither. New local receipt carries this census; shared foldStages validates and propagates it into the inline local summary only when version 2 is declared, leaving legacy receipt shapes unchanged. Closure compares local JSON bytes and inline census to the manifest, and the consumer rechecks them. Local receipt SHA-256 binds the full implementation census; no finisherModel-only shortcut. Parent independently inventories actual contributors and the reviewer checks coverage; adding a contributor after frozen review requires a new head/review/census.

futureContract.identityCapture: A trusted independent observer reads only allowlisted actual engine fields; never export the full task record, spawn_spec, notifications, descriptions, prompts, transcripts, credentials or environment. Actual inspected records use resolved_model.model_id (underscore), not guessed modelId. Archive only provider/model_id from resolved_model; absent/conflicting resolution or model != provider + '/' + model_id refuses. agent_type can be absent in actual in-process records and is stored as null, never invented. The assigned workers are GPT6.1 Sol; product checks bind observed values rather than model-name aliases. Task/session types and syntax are validated at the boundary. The source-head/review-hash envelope is observation binding, not falsely described as a native engine field.

manifestShape.localReceiptSha256: digest of exact local receipt copied by fold

futureContract.manifestRules: finishers is required even when empty; every entry has the same path/sha256 shape as author/reviewer. Reject unknown fields, malformed JSON/types/digests, missing artifacts and incomplete contributor coverage. Snapshot engine identities exactly match census and live allowlisted engine observations at production. Reviewer identity is from its own engine task, not a self-authored model/header claim. --implementer and reviewerModel header must exactly match author/reviewer engine.model; optional modern finisherModel must truthfully match its single finisher (multiple finishers use the complete manifest/census, never scalar independence). The modern review markdown's first six lines must contain exactly one plain Verdict: APPROVE, reviewedHead: <sourceHead>, reviewerModel: <actual reviewer engine.model> and reviewContractVersion: 2. This version header must agree with the JSON manifest and cannot opt into legacy without dropping modern data, which is a refusal. Legacy header acceptance remains unchanged. Existing verdict/head checks remain; duplicate/conflicting head/model/version bindings refuse.
futureContract.portableArchive: Resolve input snapshot paths relative to the manifest; require relative forward-slash paths with no absolute path, traversal or reparse escape. Copy checked minimal snapshots under the ledger evidence directory as identity-<sha256>.json and the normalized manifest as review-identity-<sha256>.json, using hashes of the exact serialized bytes (existing writeJson convention, not a new canonicalization framework). Existing identical content may be reused; any existing file with conflicting bytes refuses rather than overwrites. Receipt references are relative to the ledger directory. No per-host path or engine task-record directory is persisted in shipped identity refs. Reopen/cross-check all archives before a successful receipt; do not hash or archive full secret-bearing engine records.

receiptShape.otherFields: Retain existing unit/stage/head/reviewedHead/reviewerModel/implementerModel/outputPath/outputSha256/verdict/effort/context/laneB fields. The inline stageReceipts.review adds the exact same version and identityEvidence ref and agrees with the external review JSON. Preserve all existing merge/mainProof/tick fields.

pairedChecks: Producer validates modern identities, live engine observations, local census and all head/model/output bindings before any review evidence or ledger completion is written; bad identities leave the unit local-verified and publish no modern review/tick success.

Consumer verifies version dispatch, external review JSON and inline agreement, manifest/snapshot byte hashes, local receipt digest/census, actual output digest, role coverage and exact unit/source-head/output bindings. Identity files are mandatory in modern mode, including --no-evidence.

Reviewer task_id differs from the author and every finisher task_id, AND reviewer child_session_id differs from the author and every finisher child_session_id. Different tasks sharing a session fail; different sessions sharing a task fail; different models on the same actor still fail. Missing identities never fall back to string inequality.

Unknown/partial/downgraded modern fields, corrupt archives, swapped roles or refs, stale head/output/local receipt and inconsistent actual model/resolution fail nonzero; matching forged scalar hashes without matching observed engine records cannot pass the producer.
Legacy receipt validation is preserved unchanged; modern integrity enforcement does not retroactively demand missing engine artifacts from valid historical cross-model receipts.
futureContract.trustBoundary: Hashing proves immutable archived bytes and binding, not cryptographic engine authenticity or that a worker performed a review. Authenticity comes from observed real engine records and independent parent/reviewer comparison at authoring time, the local contributor census and normal exact-head review/CI/pinned Git delivery. A copy of a self-written JSON assertion is not engine observation. Parent must preserve the minimal observed archive in reviewed evidence and reject unaudited/self-authored substitutions. No signature service/global registry is introduced; no proof stronger than that existing trusted observation boundary is claimed.
futureContract.bootstrap: PRI itself is not exempt. After source head freeze, capture new real author/every-finisher identities and a fresh independent GPT6.1 reviewer on that exact head. Supply those observations and local census through its candidate modern closure producer and validate using its candidate consumer; unchanged consumer rejection of truthful same-model actors is the RED boundary. Before merge, run candidate validation on controlled mirrors of the real observed records and exact head; after required CI/pinned merge/exact-main proof, close PRI through the shipped candidate code at the actual merge and validate the resulting modern ledger. New candidate producer/consumer must accept that real modern review and legacy history and reject all adversarial variants. No historical example identity is approval of PRI or a future unit; no Boolean bypass or fabricated cross-model receipt is permitted.
